_about: The paper: the Wildwood Leader, its reporters, what gets printed and what doesn't.

scenes.title: A reporter from the Leader
scenes.text: A kid with a press card in his hatband stops you outside the Shamrock. The Wildwood Leader is doing a series: "Who Owns the Boardwalk?" He has a photograph of {capo.call} handing an envelope to a man in a city sanitation uniform. He would like a comment.

opinion.why: Stood behind me in the paper

choices.label: Buy the photograph ($600)

plus.why: you make it sound like his idea

choices.result: The negative went into the Shamrock's furnace. The series ran without a picture.
choices.failText: He took your money and printed it anyway, with a line about the offer.

choices.label: Have someone talk to his editor

scenes.title: The editor calls back
scenes.text: The Leader's editor telephones the house, which nobody does. The series is dead, he says. The kid has been moved to the obituaries. He would like, in return, an ad: a full page, every week, for the Season. From one of {capo.first}'s places.

choices.label: Remind him who he is talking to

scenes.title: The Leader buried you early
scenes.text: Page six of Thursday's Leader: your obituary. Fifty-one words, two of them spelled wrong, and a photograph of a different man. The printer says it was a joke by a linotype operator. The whole island read it before lunch.

choices.label: Send flowers to the linotype operator
choices.hint: A man who can laugh at his own funeral.

choices.label: Find out who paid him to set it
choices.result: It was not a joke. Somebody across the avenue paid twenty dollars for it. Now you know who wants you dead enough to print it.
choices.failText: The operator swears it was a joke. Maybe it was.
